title: Working like a Human Biologist

starterQuestions.q: Why must microscope wet mounts be prepared as single-cell-thick layers?
starterQuestions.a: To allow light to transmit through the specimen without scattering, ensuring clear focal resolution of intracellular structures.

starterQuestions.q: Why is methylene blue stain used for cheek epithelial cells?
starterQuestions.a: It binds selectively to negatively charged acidic polyanions (DNA/RNA in nuclei), creating high chromatic contrast.

starterQuestions.q: What is the formula relating Image size (I), Actual size (A), and Magnification (M)?
starterQuestions.a: Magnification (M) = Image size (I) ÷ Actual size (A) [I = A × M].

starterQuestions.q: State two mandatory conventions for scientific biological drawings.
starterQuestions.a: Single unbroken lines (no sketchiness/cross-hatching), proportional representations, and horizontal ruler-drawn label lines with no arrowheads.

starterQuestions.q: Why should a slide coverslip be lowered at a 45-degree angle?
starterQuestions.a: To displace air and prevent trapped refractive air bubbles from obscuring cellular morphology.

starterQuestions.q: How do you calculate total magnification of a compound light microscope?
starterQuestions.a: Total Magnification = Eyepiece lens magnification (typically 10×) × Objective lens magnification (e.g. 4×, 10×, 40×).

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Master optical microscope set-up, safe illumination, and systematic low-to-high magnification focusing.
objectives.application: Prepare temporary wet mounts of squamous cheek epithelium and Allium cepa epidermal tissue with differential stains.
objectives.evaluation: Execute standardized biological drawings with scale bars and evaluate sources of systematic vs random experimental error.

terminology.def: Suspending a thin specimen in liquid (water or stain) beneath a coverslip for live optical examination.
Differential stains: methylene blue highlights acidic nuclear chromatin; iodine stains starch granules and cell walls.
A transparent micrometric ruler fitted in the microscope ocular lens that must be calibrated against a stage micrometer.
Systematic calibration offsets or reading angle biases that shift all experimental measurements consistently.
